stem.en: An egg released at ovulation is not fertilised. What happens next?

text.en: The egg waits in the oviduct for many weeks, and the lining stays thick.

feedback.en: An egg stays viable for only about a day.

text.en: The lining stays for the next egg, so no period comes that month.

feedback.en: The lining is no longer needed, so it is shed.

text.en: The egg degenerates, and the lining is shed with some blood.

feedback.en: Correct. The shedding of the lining is menstruation, or a period.

text.en: The lining is shed on the same day, while the egg moves on to the uterus.

feedback.en: The lining starts to break down much later, around the end of the cycle.

explanation.en: An egg that is not fertilised stays viable for about a day and then degenerates. The thick lining is then no longer needed, so it is shed along with some blood. A period usually lasts 3 to 7 days.

hints.en: How long does an unfertilised egg stay viable?
What was the thick lining ready for?
